messages.author: d3f79de273e1d348
messages.subject: independence and segment length
parts:
Hi all,

First of all, thank you for managing the group, making packages and guides! Distance and DSM are of big help, so Thank you so much!.
My question has arose from reading previous questions in the group, here I go...

Consider the situation where I want to build a DSM for my study area, and to do that I'm using data that was collected from line transects with this design:
I have "A" transects of length "B". Each transect was walked "C" times, and was divided in segments of length "D".

When organizing the data for the analysis: which of these 2 options is the correct way?:
a. The length of each transect should be "BxC", therefore the length of each segment should be "DxC".
b. I could consider each transect and repetition as "independent" from each other, therefore I could think I have "AxC" transects with segments of length "D".

In the forum, I have read that independence is never reached in the real world, because it is difficult that adjacent segments are independent from each other.

So, could be "option b" correct?

Thank you!
Regards
Nicolas

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] independence and segment length
parts:
Nicholas

Good question, very clearly asked.

In most instances we have investigated, the answer is "b".  That stems largely from the ecosystem investigated was marine (literally quite fluid; animals found in a segment on one visit are no more likely to be in that segment on a repeat visit), temporal spacing of the visits was relatively large (e.g. yearly repeat surveys) and "dynamic" (time-varying) covariates in the detection function, density surface model, or both.
